overall_justification: V2 is now a watchable, followable story with real VO, one clock, a reference-grade climax cut and a breathing workshop turn. But the payoff and the emotional hinge still contradict themselves on screen (double finish, invisible screwdriver set-down, laughing shout faces, card-like LED), and the bodies are mostly paper dolls.

delta.note: Every auditor moved up 1.5-3.0. The V1 prediction for V2 was 7.0 and actual is 6.0. The gap is in the fixes that only half landed (S066 bench under the letterbox, S093 wrong lane, S091b card, 0:01/0:02 clock) and in animation, which needs per-shot acting work rather than lib passes.

verdict: V2 is the first cut a stranger could watch to the end and follow. The VO fix brought back the hook, the proof, the dialogue and the timing (5:53, 0 overlaps). The climax is now cut at action tempo, and the workshop turn finally has silence and room. It does not ship yet, because the beats that carry the meaning still contradict the picture. The robot finishes twice while the clock goes 0:01→0:02. The 'swerve' never threatens the barrier. The cause beat (S091b) is an abstract blue card. Noah's set-down of the screwdriver happens under the letterbox. In the key shout exchange, both boys look like they are laughing. In the working tree the animator has already fixed most of the story, rhythm and lighting items, and has started on logic and animation: clock and finish, S066 bench, shout mouth, numeric sit, idle sway, smoothed lip-sync, S091b chassis, S093 overhead swerve, music stops, room tone. One new P0 came out of this review: the overhead route cuts through barrier 3, which S094 now shows during the payoff. V3 priorities: finish and verify the P0s, then the remaining acting (S065 oblivious Eli, S058, gestures, S054b), the warm payoff light and the hall-exchange angles. No script changes. The WIP timeline is 350.2 s with 122 shots.

conflicts_resolved.topic: S093 swerve staging: logic wanted a locked LOW with a depth yaw and the barrier occluding, animation wanted a scaleX yaw fake, story wanted a same-lane bank, and the animator built a close overhead.
conflicts_resolved.decision: Keep the TOP-close overhead and drop the LOW variant.
conflicts_resolved.why: An overhead is the only angle where 'went around the barrier instead of into it' is unambiguous in about 1.6 s. It rhymes with the S077 failure map (same barrier, opposite outcome), and it avoids the 2D-rotate hop entirely. The S092 GFX sits between S093 and the S094 overhead, so there are no back-to-back TOPs. Condition: the route must clear every barrier (new P0 on barrier 3).

conflicts_resolved.topic: S013 landing: animation called it fixed (motion reads), logic called it a headstand (held frame).
conflicts_resolved.decision: P2 polish. The torso ends horizontal at ground level with a bounce, and the shot stays ≥2.2 s.
conflicts_resolved.why: Both are right: the fall reads in motion, but the 1.5 s hold is a headstand silhouette. Fixing the final frame costs little and doesn't touch the timing.

conflicts_resolved.topic: Rhythm wants Acts 1-2 punch cuts under 1.5 s (minShot 1.3-1.4, w .6-.7). Animation wants room for the action (S013 fall, S036 trap) to read.
conflicts_resolved.decision: Shorten only reaction and comedy cuts (S010, S015, S032, S078) and lengthen S022. Leave the S013 and S036 action shots at ≥2.2 s.
conflicts_resolved.why: Cut contrast comes from short reactions next to readable actions. Clipping a gag before it lands is worse than a 2.2 s shot.

conflicts_resolved.topic: S067: rhythm proposed a dark door-frame FG with Noah walking toward the lens. Logic and story wanted Eli visibly back-turned and oblivious. The animator reversed the setup.
conflicts_resolved.decision: Accept the working-tree staging: the ENV.workshopRev door wall, Eli as a back-turned FG, Noah walking to the lit door, the door closing.
conflicts_resolved.why: It satisfies all three: a different wall and a pull-out against S068's push, so no jump cut. Eli can't see Noah leave. The door close is motivated in picture. Update the S067 desc to match.

conflicts_resolved.topic: S106 callback: story offered either Eli on the bench next to Noah or a TOP insert. Logic wanted Eli's stool flush with the keys.
conflicts_resolved.decision: The S106b TOP insert (done) carries the musical payoff. Moving the stool flush is a P2 so the wide agrees with the insert.
conflicts_resolved.why: The insert mirrors S002/S105 exactly (strongest callback), and the melody is trimmed so 'ten hours' plays dry.

conflicts_resolved.topic: L069 'crossed the finish line just before the timer ran out': drop it, or move it after the horn.
conflicts_resolved.why: The picture now carries 0:01 → crossing → horn → WINNER. The runtime stays at 350.2 s, inside 5:30-6:00.

conflicts_resolved.topic: tension_competition overrun: stop at S087 and restart at S089, or start the cue later.
conflicts_resolved.why: It turns an accidental fade into a deliberate hush that mirrors S066, and the restart lands on 'What do I do?!'.

conflicts_resolved.topic: S061 lighting: lighting wanted the hanging lamp as the visible source. Rhythm wanted a true reverse plate.

conflicts_resolved.why: The new plate has its own motivated sources, and the cool reverse versus the warm window side splits the argument by speaker. Follow-up: S065 rims must switch to cool (in the S065 fix).
